subject: Atrial fibrillation, also called afib or AF,
object: a heart rhythm problem in which the heartbeat is not steady.
source_quote: Atrial fibrillation (sometimes called afib or AF) is a type of heart rhythm problem where your heartbeat is not steady.

subject: The main symptoms of atrial fibrillation
object: an irregular, unsteady pulse; a sudden pounding, racing, fluttering, skipping or missed heartbeat lasting a few seconds up to a few minutes; a heartbeat faster than 100 beats per minute; feeling very tired; difficulty exercising; chest pain or tightness; and breathlessness, lightheadedness, dizziness or feeling faint.
source_quote: The main symptoms of atrial fibrillation are: an irregular heartbeat, where your pulse is not steady suddenly feeling like your heart is pounding, racing, fluttering, skipping or missing a beat (heart palpitations) – this may last for a few seconds up to a few minutes a heartbeat faster than 100 beats per minute feeling very tired finding it harder to exercise chest pain or tightness feeling short of breath, lightheaded, dizzy or like you might faint

subject: Atrial fibrillation
object: no symptoms and is discovered during a routine check-up or tests for something else.
source_quote: Sometimes there are no symptoms, and atrial fibrillation is found as part of a routine check-up or when you're having tests for something else.

subject: Symptoms of atrial fibrillation
object: start and stop on their own in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation or stop after treatment in persistent atrial fibrillation; over time, symptoms may always be present in permanent atrial fibrillation.
source_quote: If you do get symptoms, they may start and stop on their own (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation) or stop after treatment (persistent atrial fibrillation). Over time, you may always have symptoms (permanent atrial fibrillation).

subject: If a GP thinks a person could have atrial fibrillation,
object: to a heart specialist, who at the appointment will ask about symptoms and check the heart rate.
source_quote: If a GP thinks you could have atrial fibrillation, they will refer you to a heart specialist (cardiologist). At your appointment, they will ask about your symptoms and check your heart rate.

subject: Testing for atrial fibrillation
object: the heart rhythm and whether something else could be causing the symptoms; tests may include an electrocardiogram, echocardiogram, chest X-ray and blood tests.
source_quote: Tests for atrial fibrillation You will also have tests to see if anything else could be causing your symptoms and to check your heart rhythm. Tests may include: an electrocardiogram (ECG) an echocardiogram (echo) a chest X-ray blood tests

subject: For atrial fibrillation, medicines
object: to control the rate and rhythm of the heart, such as beta blockers, and to lower the risk of blood clots or stroke, using anticoagulants.
source_quote: Treatment for atrial fibrillation You may be given medicine to: control the rate and rhythm of your heart, such as beta blockers lower the risk of blood clots or stroke (anticoagulants)

subject: Other possible treatments for atrial fibrillation
object: ablation, using burning, freezing or high-energy electrical pulses to destroy a section of the heart; electrical cardioversion to reset the heart rhythm; and fitting a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator.
source_quote: Other possible treatments for atrial fibrillation include: burning, freezing or using high-energy electrical pulses to destroy a section of your heart (ablation) using electricity to reset your heart rhythm (electrical cardioversion) having a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) fitted

subject: Atrial fibrillation
object: by another health condition or medicine; in these cases, treating that condition or stopping the medicine can improve symptoms.
source_quote: Sometimes atrial fibrillation can be caused by another health condition or medicine. In these cases, treating the condition or stopping the medicine can improve the symptoms.

subject: People with atrial fibrillation
object: continue most usual activities, including exercise, but should avoid intense exercise, try not to exercise while having atrial fibrillation symptoms and check with their doctor if unsure what exercise they can do.
source_quote: How atrial fibrillation affects your life You should be able to carry on doing most things as usual, including exercise. But avoid intense exercise and try not to exercise when you're having symptoms of atrial fibrillation. Check with your doctor if you're not sure what exercise you can do.

subject: Atrial fibrillation
object: a problem in the electrical system that makes the heart beat.
source_quote: Atrial fibrillation is caused by a problem with the electrical system that makes your heart beat.

subject: Atrial fibrillation
object: another condition such as high blood pressure; heart failure, mitral valve problems or Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome; a heart attack; chronic kidney disease; an overactive thyroid; diabetes; or sleep apnoea.
source_quote: Atrial fibrillation can also be caused by another condition such as: high blood pressure heart conditions like heart failure, mitral valve problems or Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome a heart attack chronic kidney disease an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism) diabetes sleep apnoea

subject: Anyone can develop atrial fibrillation, but it
object: in people aged 55 or older, men, people living with obesity or overweight, smokers, people taking certain medicines such as levothyroxine, lithium or asthma medicines such as salbutamol, and people doing endurance sports such as long-distance running, cycling or skiing.
source_quote: Causes of atrial fibrillation Anyone can get it, but you may be more likely to get it if: you're aged 55 or older you're a man you're living with obesity or overweight you smoke you take certain medicines, such as levothyroxine, lithium or some asthma medicines like salbutamol you do endurance sports like long-distance running, cycling or skiing

subject: The emergency advice on the NHS atrial fibrillation page
object: you currently have a fast or irregular heartbeat with chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, feeling or being sick, fainting or dizziness or falling over, a severe headache, one-sided facial or body weakness or numbness, blurred vision or loss of sight, or confusion or difficulty speaking; do not drive yourself to A&E, and the person answering 999 will advise what to do.
source_quote: Atrial fibrillation Immediate action required: Call 999 if: You currently have a fast or irregular heartbeat, and any of these symptoms: chest pain shortness of breath sweating feeling or being sick fainting, feeling dizzy or falling over a severe headache weakness or numbness on one side of your face or body blurred vision or loss of sight confusion or difficulty speaking Do not drive yourself to A&E. The person you speak to at 999 will give you advice about what to do.

subject: Atrial fibrillation
relation: currently has no cure, but treatment should
object: help manage symptoms and lower the risk of complications such as blood clots, stroke and heart failure.
source_quote: There is currently no cure for atrial fibrillation, but treatment should help manage the symptoms and lower the risk of complications like blood clots, stroke and heart failure.

subject: Several mechanisms involving electrical and structural remodelling of atrial tissue
relation: have been proposed to contribute to
object: atrial fibrillation, and fibrosis has been studied thoroughly, confirming its significant role in this process.
source: Article: Sagris M, Vardas EP, Theofilis P et al. Atrial Fibrillation: Pathogenesis, Predisposing Factors, and Genetics. International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2021
source_quote: Several mechanisms have been postulated to play a role in the development of AF, through both the electrical and structural remodeling of the atrial tissue. Among them, fibrosis has been studied thoroughly, confirming its significant role in this process.

subject: Fibrosis is a significant factor maintaining atrial fibrillation, and it
object: increased fibroblasts or myofibroblasts and extracellular matrix in fibrotic tissue disrupt myocardial-bundle continuity and interfere with cardiomyocyte gap-junction formation, leading to conduction abnormalities, slower conduction and eventually unidirectional conduction blocks.
source: Article: Sagris M, Vardas EP, Theofilis P et al. Atrial Fibrillation: Pathogenesis, Predisposing Factors, and Genetics. International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2021
source_quote: Fibrosis has been established as a significant factor maintaining atrial fibrillation. It has been proposed that the increased population of fibroblasts/myofibroblasts present in the fibrotic tissue and the increased deposition of ECM disrupt the myocardial bundles continuity, interfering with the gap-junction formation among cardiomyocytes. This event leads to conduction abnormalities, slowing conduction velocity and eventually forming unidirectional conduction blocks .

subject: Accumulating evidence
object: the onset and maintenance of atrial fibrillation; inflammation contributes to structural and electrophysiological atrial remodelling that forms the basis for the disease.
source: Article: Sagris M, Vardas EP, Theofilis P et al. Atrial Fibrillation: Pathogenesis, Predisposing Factors, and Genetics. International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2021
source_quote: Inflammation has been linked to the onset and maintenance of atrial fibrillation, according to accumulating evidence. Inflammation contributes to the atrial remodelling involving both structural and electrophysiological alterations that form the basis for the disease.

subject: Atrial fibrillation
object: thromboembolic risk, including ischaemic stroke, regardless of its temporal pattern; without appropriate treatment, ischaemic stroke risk is increased five-fold, and one in every five strokes is linked to atrial fibrillation.
source: Article: Rienstra M, Tzeis S, Bunting KV et al. Spotlight on the 2024 ESC/EACTS management of atrial fibrillation guidelines: 10 novel key aspects. Europace 2024
source_quote: Atrial fibrillation significantly heightens the risk of thromboembolism, including ischaemic stroke, regardless of the temporal pattern of AF.,, Without appropriate treatment, the risk of ischaemic stroke in patients with AF is elevated five-fold, and one in every five strokes is linked to AF.

subject: In intermittent atrial fibrillation,
relation: symptoms and heart rhythm correlate poorly
object: because symptoms are not specific and may result from coexisting comorbidities.
source: Article: Rienstra M, Tzeis S, Bunting KV et al. Spotlight on the 2024 ESC/EACTS management of atrial fibrillation guidelines: 10 novel key aspects. Europace 2024
source_quote: The correlation between symptoms and heart rhythm is poor in patients with intermittent AF, since patient symptoms are not specific and may be due to coexistent comorbidities.

subject: Atrial fibrosis
object: a significant pathophysiological component of atrial fibrillation, linked with recurrence, resistance to medication and complications.
source: Article: Sagris M, Vardas EP, Theofilis P et al. Atrial Fibrillation: Pathogenesis, Predisposing Factors, and Genetics. International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2021
source_quote: Atrial fibrosis has emerged as a significant pathophysiological component, with links to AF recurrences, resistance to medication, and complications .
